cond_0001.intro: The Manufacturing Engineer II has the opportunity to actively participate in the technological transformation through robotics and automation of a highly respected top quality marine product manufacturer. The position carries responsibility for planning, tooling, operations and engineering teams to develop cost effective, and robust solutions to manufacturing problems developing or adapting methods to produce discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The MEI is also responsible for design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Coordinates vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools, assembly processes
Versed in the principles and holds responsibility for implementing Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods
Develops PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity to ensure safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items
Conducts Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and develops detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes
Develops process flow maps and identifies potential bottle necks and costly operations and makes recommendations relative to quality, tooling and manufacturing processes
Conducts in-depth studies relative to justification of equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, system standardization of parts, components assemblies and materials
Prepares and implements changes in existing plant layout and capital investments
Supports automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion
Conducts time and motion studies. Assists in determining capacity and production standards
Estimates and validates production capacity via pilot builds and run at rate studies to establish labor content of end items
Develops process change plans, validates change effectiveness and implements changes in processes, time standards and bills of material
Coordinates Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery and controls.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Facility using solid modeling software
Knowledge of 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD)
Functional understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc)
Functional knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding
Project management experience with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments
Read and author PLC ladder logic
Preferred Requirements
Solid modeling software experience with Creo Parametric (Pro/Engineer WF5)
Advanced use of typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint); intermediate use of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform
Knowledge of high level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java)

The position carries responsibility for planning, tooling, operations and engineering teams to develop cost effective, and robust solutions to manufacturing problems developing or adapting methods to produce discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The MEI is also responsible for design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0011.responsibilities:
Coordinates vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools, assembly processes
Versed in the principles and holds responsibility for implementing Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods
Develops PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity to ensure safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items
Conducts Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and develops detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes
Develops process flow maps and identifies potential bottle necks and costly operations and makes recommendations relative to quality, tooling and manufacturing processes
Conducts in-depth studies relative to justification of equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, system standardization of parts, components assemblies and materials
Prepares and implements changes in existing plant layout and capital investments
Supports automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion
Conducts time and motion studies. Assists in determining capacity and production standards
Estimates and validates production capacity via pilot builds and run at rate studies to establish labor content of end items
Develops process change plans, validates change effectiveness and implements changes in processes, time standards and bills of material
Coordinates Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery and controls.
cond_0011.requirements:
Strong command of solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5] preferred)
Proficiency in 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD preferred)
Solid understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc)
Advanced knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding
Proven track record in project management with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments
Advanced expertise in typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint); deep knowledge of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform a plus
Proficiency in high level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java) preferred
Demonstrated expertise reading and authoring PLC ladder logic

Develop process change plans, validate change effectiveness, and implement changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Coordinate daily with the Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls.

cond_0177.intro: The Manufacturing Engineer has the opportunity to actively take part in the technological transformation through robotics and automation at [Company name masked], a marine product manufacturer. The role carries responsibility for working closely with planning, tooling, operations, and engineering teams to develop cost-effective, robust solutions to manufacturing problems, and regularly communicating with vendors, contractors, and internal groups to develop methods for producing discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The role is also responsible for design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0177.responsibilities:
Coordinates vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools and assembly processes, staying in regular contact throughout the process.
Versed in the principles and holds responsibility for implementing Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods.
Develops PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity to ensure safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items.
Conducts Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and develops detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes.
Develops process flow maps, identifies potential bottlenecks and costly operations, and actively communicates recommendations relative to quality, tooling, and manufacturing processes to relevant teams.
Conducts in-depth studies relative to justification of equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, and system standardization of parts, components, assemblies, and materials.
Prepares and implements changes in existing plant layout and capital investments.
Supports automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion, connecting with stakeholders at each stage.
Conducts time and motion studies. Assists in determining capacity and production standards.
Estimates and validates production capacity via pilot builds and run at rate studies to establish labor content of end items.
Develops process change plans, validates change effectiveness, and implements changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Coordinates Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls, initiating discussions to keep all parties aligned.
cond_0177.requirements:
Facility using solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5] preferred).
Knowledge of 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD preferred).
Functional understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc).
Functional knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding.
Project management experience with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments.
Advanced use of typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint). Intermediate use of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform a plus.
Knowledge of high level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java) preferred.
Read and author PLC ladder logic.
cond_0177.values: We value work that reflects care for people and consideration for its wider impact. We aim to make decisions in ways that are responsible, fair, and respectful.

The position carries responsibility for planning, tooling, operations and engineering teams to develop cost effective, and robust solutions to manufacturing problems developing or adapting methods to produce discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The MEI is also responsible for design and procurement of assembly. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of manufacturing processes and automation systems.
cond_0202.responsibilities:
Coordinates vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools, assembly processes
Versed in the principles and holds responsibility for implementing Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods
Develops PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity to ensure safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items
Conducts Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and develops detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes
Develops process flow maps and identifies potential bottle necks and costly operations and makes recommendations relative to quality, tooling and manufacturing processes
Conducts in-depth studies relative to justification of equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, system standardization of parts, components assemblies and materials
Prepares and implements changes in existing plant layout and capital investments
Supports automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion
Conducts time and motion studies. Assists in determining capacity and production standards
Estimates and validates production capacity via pilot builds and run at rate studies to establish labor content of end items
Develops process change plans, validates change effectiveness and implements changes in processes, time standards and bills of material
Coordinates Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery and controls.
cond_0202.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Facility using solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5] preferred)
Knowledge of 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD preferred)
Functional understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc)
Functional knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding
Project management experience with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments
Read and author PLC ladder logic
Preferred Requirements
Advanced use of typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint); intermediate use of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform a plus
Knowledge of high level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java)

The role carries responsibility for working closely with planning, tooling, operations, and engineering teams to develop cost-effective, robust solutions to manufacturing problems, and regularly communicating with vendors, contractors, and internal groups to develop methods for producing discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The role is also responsible for design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0267.responsibilities:
Coordinates vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools and assembly processes, staying in regular contact throughout the process.
Versed in the principles and holds responsibility for implementing Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods.
Develops PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity to ensure safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items.
Conducts Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and develops detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes.
Develops process flow maps, identifies potential bottlenecks and costly operations, and actively communicates recommendations relative to quality, tooling, and manufacturing processes to relevant teams.
Conducts in-depth studies relative to justification of equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, and system standardization of parts, components, assemblies, and materials.
Prepares and implements changes in existing plant layout and capital investments.
Supports automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion, connecting with stakeholders at each stage.
Conducts time and motion studies. Assists in determining capacity and production standards.
Estimates and validates production capacity via pilot builds and run at rate studies to establish labor content of end items.
Develops process change plans, validates change effectiveness, and implements changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Coordinates Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls, initiating discussions to keep all parties aligned.
cond_0267.requirements:
Facility using solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5] preferred).
Knowledge of 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD preferred).
Functional understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc).
Functional knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding.
Project management experience with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments.
Advanced use of typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint). Intermediate use of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform a plus.
Knowledge of high level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java) preferred.
Read and author PLC ladder logic.

cond_0278.intro: The Manufacturing Engineer II will own a meaningful role in the technological transformation through robotics and automation at [Company name masked], a top-quality marine product manufacturer. This position drives responsibility across planning, tooling, operations, and engineering teams to deliver cost-effective, robust solutions to manufacturing problems — developing or adapting methods to produce discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. This role also takes ownership of design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0278.responsibilities:
Lead coordination with vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools and assembly processes.
Direct implementation of Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods.
Develop PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity, ensuring safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items.
Execute Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis; develop detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes.
Develop process flow maps, identify bottlenecks and costly operations, and make recommendations on quality, tooling, and manufacturing processes.
Conduct in-depth studies to justify equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, and system standardization of parts, components, assemblies, and materials.
Prepare and implement changes in existing plant layout and capital investments.
Drive automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion.
Conduct time and motion studies; determine capacity and production standards.
Estimate and validate production capacity via pilot builds and run-at-rate studies to establish labor content of end items.
Develop process change plans, validate change effectiveness, and implement changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Lead coordination with Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls.
cond_0278.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Facility using solid modeling software
Knowledge of 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD)
Functional understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc.)
Functional knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, and extruding
Project management experience with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments
Ability to read and author PLC ladder logic
Preferred Requirements
Experience with Creo Parametric (Pro/Engineer WF5)
Advanced use of MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint; intermediate use of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform
Knowledge of high-level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java)

Develop process change plans, validate change effectiveness, and implement changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Coordinate daily with the Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls.

The role involves working closely with planning, tooling, operations, and engineering teams to develop cost-effective, robust solutions to manufacturing problems, and to develop or adapt methods for producing discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The role also carries responsibility for design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0546.responsibilities:
Coordinate regularly with vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools and assembly processes.
Apply Lean and Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods and take initiative in implementing them across the floor.
Develop PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity, ensuring safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items.
Conduct Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis; develop detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk in end item assembly processes.
Develop process flow maps, identify bottlenecks and costly operations, and actively communicate recommendations on quality, tooling, and manufacturing processes to relevant teams.
Conduct in-depth studies to justify equipment purchases and modifications, work simplification, and system standardization of parts, components, assemblies, and materials.
Prepare and implement changes in existing plant layout and capital investments.
Support automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion, staying in regular contact with project stakeholders throughout.
Conduct time and motion studies; assist in determining capacity and production standards.
Estimate and validate production capacity via pilot builds and run-at-rate studies to establish labor content of end items.
Develop process change plans, validate change effectiveness, and implement changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Coordinate daily with the Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls.

Functional understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc.)

Facility using solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5])

cond_0557.responsibilities:
Lead coordination with vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools and assembly processes.
Drive implementation of Lean and Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods.
Develop PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity, ensuring safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items.
Execute Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis; develop detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes.
Develop process flow maps, identify bottlenecks and costly operations, and make decisions on quality, tooling, and manufacturing processes.
Conduct in-depth studies to justify equipment purchases and modifications, work simplification, and system standardization of parts, components, assemblies, and materials.
Prepare and implement changes in existing plant layout and capital investments.
Drive automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion.
Conduct time and motion studies; determine capacity and production standards.
Estimate and validate production capacity via pilot builds and run-at-rate studies to establish labor content of end items.
Develop process change plans, validate change effectiveness, and implement changes in processes, time standards, and bills of material.
Direct Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop, and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery, and controls.
cond_0557.requirements:
Facility using solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5] preferred).

Functional knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding.
Project management experience with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments.
Advanced use of typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint); intermediate use of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform a plus.

cond_0605.intro: The Manufacturing Engineer II has the exciting opportunity to actively participate in the technological transformation through robotics and automation of a highly respected top quality marine product manufacturer. The position carries responsibility for planning, tooling, operations and engineering teams to develop cost effective, and robust solutions to manufacturing problems developing or adapting methods to produce discrete and repetitive style production parts and assemblies. The MEI is also responsible for design and procurement of assembly.
cond_0605.responsibilities:
Coordinates vendors and outside contractors in the development of tools, assembly processes
Versed in the principles and holds responsibility for implementing Lean & Continuous Improvement manufacturing methods
Develops PLC logic and SCADA to control and capture production activity to ensure safe and poka-yoke proofing of assembly production end items
Conducts Machine and Process Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and develops detection and prevention methods and control plans to reduce risk and liability in end item assembly processes
Develops process flow maps and identifies potential bottle necks and costly operations and makes recommendations relative to quality, tooling and manufacturing processes
Conducts in-depth studies relative to justification of equipment purchases/modifications, work simplification, system standardization of parts, components assemblies and materials
Prepares and implements changes in existing plant layout and capital investments
Supports automation and robotic development projects from inception to completion
Conducts time and motion studies. Assists in determining capacity and production standards
Estimates and validates production capacity via pilot builds and run at rate studies to establish labor content of end items
Develops process change plans, validates change effectiveness and implements changes in processes, time standards and bills of material
Coordinates Tool Room, Suppliers, Machine Shop and Maintenance in the design and development of new tooling, fixtures, nests, machinery and controls.
cond_0605.requirements:
Strong command of solid modeling software (Creo Parametric [Pro/Engineer WF5] preferred)
Proficiency in 2-D modeling software (AutoCAD preferred)
Solid understanding of measurement equipment (calipers, micrometers, comparator, etc)
Advanced knowledge of manufacturing processes including turning, milling, molding, casting, extruding
Proven track record in project management with demonstrated ability to meet required timeline commitments
Advanced expertise in typical office software (MS Word, MS Excel, MS PowerPoint); deep knowledge of MS Access or equivalent relational database platform a plus
Proficiency in high level control system programming languages (VB, C++, Java) preferred
Demonstrated expertise reading and authoring PLC ladder logic
